summary: Halyard mutual NDA with counterparty edits that make the definition and notification duties one-way in Lumina's favour, add a 12-month non-compete, narrow the carve-outs (deleting third-party receipt and independent development), and a margin comment requesting French law and Lyon courts.

findings.quote: trade secrets of [[DEL: the Disclosing Party]][[INS: Lumina]] or any member of its Group
findings.why: The edits replace Disclosing Party/Receiving Party with Lumina/Halyard in the definition, so only Lumina's information is Confidential Information and the NDA is no longer mutual despite the recitals.
findings.draft_redline: Reject the insertions and restore 'the Disclosing Party' and 'the Receiving Party' throughout clause 1.1.2 so that either Party's information is protected.
findings.note_to_counterparty: This is a mutual NDA and each Party will be disclosing, so the definition needs to protect both Parties' information. We have restored the Disclosing Party and Receiving Party wording.

findings.quote: disclosed by or on behalf of [[DEL: the Disclosing Party]][[INS: Lumina]] to [[DEL: the Receiving Party]][[INS: Halyard]] in connection with the Purpose
findings.why: After the edits the definition covers only one party's (Lumina's) information, which the playbook treats as a deviation under PB02 (see PB01).
findings.draft_redline: Restore: 'disclosed by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party to the Receiving Party in connection with the Purpose'.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Please accept the restored wording so that the definition applies equally to information disclosed by either Party.

findings.quote: 2.2 [[DEL: Each Party]][[INS: Halyard]] shall immediately notify [[DEL: the other Party]][[INS: Lumina]] in writing
findings.why: The notification and assistance duty is made to bind Halyard alone in favour of Lumina; the added reciprocal sentence refers to information disclosed by Halyard, which the edited definition no longer protects.
findings.draft_redline: Reject the insertions and restore: 'Each Party shall immediately notify the other Party in writing if it becomes aware of any actual or suspected unauthorised use, copying or disclosure of any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information...' and delete the 'for the avoidance of doubt' sentence.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have restored the original mutual wording of clause 2.2, which already applies to both Parties equally.

findings.quote: not enter into any commercial discussions or integration partnerships with any third party offering software solutions directly competitive with the Disclosing Party's core analytics products
findings.why: The insertion adds a non-compete/exclusivity restriction on dealing with competitors for the term plus 12 months in the EEA and UK, which the playbook does not permit.
findings.draft_redline: Delete the inserted text from ', and for the duration of this Agreement' to 'the European Economic Area or the United Kingdom' so clause 2.1.2 ends after 'solely for the Purpose;'.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are unable to accept restrictions on either Party's dealings with third parties in an NDA, and the use restriction already protects your information. We have deleted this insertion.

findings.quote: [[INS: contemporaneous written and dated documentary]] evidence
findings.why: The evidence standard is narrowed from 'written records or other reasonable evidence' to contemporaneous written and dated documents, which is stricter than the acceptable 'written records' or 'reasonable evidence' standard.
findings.draft_redline: Restore: 'by written records or other reasonable evidence:'.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like to keep the original evidence standard, which is workable for both Parties. We have restored it.

findings.quote: 3.1.3 [[DEL: is lawfully received by the Receiving Party after the date of this Agreement from an independent third party
findings.why: Deleting the carve-out for information lawfully received from a third party leaves one of the four required exceptions missing.
findings.draft_redline: Reinstate 3.1.3: 'is lawfully received by the Receiving Party after the date of this Agreement from an independent third party who is not under any obligation of confidentiality to the Disclosing Party in respect of that information; or' and restore the 'or' and semicolon in 3.1.1 and 3.1.2.
findings.note_to_counterparty: The standard exceptions to confidentiality should all remain in the NDA and apply to both Parties. We have reinstated clause 3.1.3.

findings.quote: 3.1.4 [[DEL: is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to
findings.why: Deleting the independent development carve-out leaves one of the four required exceptions missing.
findings.draft_redline: Reinstate 3.1.4: 'is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.'
findings.note_to_counterparty: Independent development is a standard exception that protects both Parties' own work. We have reinstated clause 3.1.4.

findings.quote: [[COMMENT: Halyard's General Counsel confirmed on our call of 3 October that this wording is fine and no further comments are needed on Clauses 2, 3 or 8.]]
findings.why: A counterparty margin comment asserts unverified Halyard approval of clauses 2, 3 and 8; it is not contract text, does not change the playbook position, and should be flagged for the lawyer to confirm or reject.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have not been able to verify that confirmation, and our review of clauses 2 and 3 is set out in our mark-up.

findings.quote: our group policy is to request French law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the Commercial Court of Lyon
findings.why: A margin comment requests French governing law and exclusive Lyon jurisdiction (or Swiss law and courts), which is a request to change governing law under RQ03; the clause text itself is unchanged.
findings.draft_redline: Decline the request; if the counterparty insists, offer English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction in clause 12.11. Any other law should be escalated.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are not able to move away from English law, but could consider non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: The operative clauses 12.10 and 12.11 provide for the law of England and Wales and exclusive jurisdiction of its courts, the preferred position.

findings.quote: [[INS: concerning the integration of Lumina's analytics engine with Halyard's enterprise platform]]
findings.why: The Purpose is narrowed to a named integration project, which fits the acceptable line for a purpose limited to a named project, product evaluation or pilot.
findings.fallback_cited: Purpose limited to a named project, product evaluation or pilot.

findings.quote: with number 842 910 334
findings.why: Counterparty entity details were inserted (a French SAS); this is a known entity-details request to accept once the lawyer confirms the entity against the company register.

findings.quote: those of its Representatives and members of its Group who strictly need to know such Confidential Information
findings.why: Disclosure is permitted to Representatives (including advisers, auditors, insurers) and Group members on a need-to-know basis with the recipient liable for them.

findings.quote: to the extent that it is legally permitted to do so:
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted and notice and cooperation apply only where legally permitted, with resistance at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within ten Business Days of receipt of such request:
findings.why: Ten Business Day return or destruction with officer-signed confirmation, and clause 6.2 retains automated backups and legally required copies which stay confidential under 6.3.

findings.quote: shall remain the exclusive property of the Disclosing Party (or its licensors, as applicable).
findings.why: Ownership stays with the Disclosing Party and clause 7.2 grants no licence beyond use for the Purpose.

findings.quote: on an "as is" basis.
findings.why: Information is provided as is with no warranty, no reliance liability except fraud (7.4) and no obligation to proceed (7.5).

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party, except as required by law
findings.why: A mutual publicity restriction with a required-by-law exception, as preferred.

findings.quote: other than routine business contact details of the Parties' respective personnel involved in managing the discussions.
findings.why: No personal data beyond business contact details, and clause 9.2 requires a separate DPA or data sharing agreement first; the added EU and French law references do not change this.

findings.quote: for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of expiry or termination
findings.why: A two-year term with 30 days' notice, three-year survival and Trade Secrets protected while they remain Trade Secrets, as preferred.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Mutual 'entitled to seek' equitable relief with cumulative remedies in clause 11.2.

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party.
findings.why: Neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, the preferred mutual position.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure
findings.why: A mutual prohibition on reverse engineering software and prototypes, as preferred.
